The PassDown node can be thought of as a Basin without storage. It fully 'passes-down' flow, so the sum of the inflow is always equal to the sum of the outflow. As such, the PassDown node does not need any profile information. The general concept is:
- The PassDown node receives flow from other nodes which provide flow: connector nodes, FlowBoundary or other PassDown nodes
- The PassDown node directs this flow to flow receiving nodes: Basins, level boundaries, terminals, user demands or other PassDown nodes

PassDown nodes can be chained arbitrarily, as long as there are no loops (and at the moment we do not support confluences of multiple PassDown nodes into a PassDown node). Over such chains, which are subgraphs of the model consisting of PassDown and potentially UserDemand nodes, flow travels instantaneously.

# Connectivity rules

The PassDown node has some specific connectivity rules:
- A maximum of 1 UserDemand node can abstract from a PassDown node.
- A UserDemand node cannot abstract from Basin(s) and a PassDown node simultaneously.
- Since a PassDown node cannot accumulate water, it always needs one or more outflow links. If the PassDown node flows into a UserDemand node, there must be another outflow link to a different node type, because the inflow to the PassDown can be larger than the demand and the remainder needs somewhere to go.
